THE HEADLINES::

 

  1. National Unity Day being celebrated today, marking 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

 

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi to take part in celebrations at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat today; To also launch development projects worth over 400 crore rupees.

 

  1. Centre forms a high-level committee to recommend reforms in banking sector for Viksit Bharat, 2047.

 

  1. ISRO successfully launches next generation satellite NVS-03, bolstering country’s indigenous navigation capabilities.

<><><> 

 

 

The nation is paying homage to the great freedom fighter Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, on his 151st birth anniversary today. The day is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, or National Unity Day. President Droupadi Murmu and Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan today paid floral tributes to the Iron Man of India, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, at his statue at Patel Chowk in New Delhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also paid tributes to saying Sardar Patel dedicated his life to building a strong, prosperous and capable India.  Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj also paid floral tributes to the great national leader. Later Union Home Minister Amit Shah flagged off the ‘Run for Unity’ at the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium to mark Rashtriya Ekta Diwas. Speaking at the event, Mr Shah said He was a great personality who not only transformed the nation’s history but also shaped its very geography. He said India stands proudly on the global stage today because of the strong foundations laid by Sardar Patel.

 

“Popularly known as the Iron Man of India, Sardar Patel served as country’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister and played a historic role in integrating more than 560 princely states to build a united and strong India.Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrates his immense contribution to the political integration and unity of the country. The occasion also serves as a reminder of the importance of national unity, integrity, security and harmony in India’s diverse and vibrant society.

Government institutions, schools and colleges are organising unity pledges, cultural programmes and awareness activities across the country to commemorate Sardar Patel’s ideals and legacy. On the occasion, the Run for Unity is also being organised at various places across the country to spread the message of national integration, peace and brotherhood. SANJEEV JASROTIA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

 

 

<><><>

 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over 400 crore rupees at Ekta Nagar in Narmada district of Gujarat this morning. The projects include a sewage and water treatment plant, facade lighting, the upgradation of Narmada Ghat, and the Rainforest, among others.

On the second and final day of his visit to Gujarat, Mr Modi will also offer floral tributes at the Statue of Unity to mark the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Later in the evening, the Prime Minister will participate in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations on the occasion.

 

 

<><><>

 

 

Akashvani will broadcast tonight the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan. The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network at 9:30 PM on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary. Delivering the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, the Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister said, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will jointly flag off the new Vande Bharat Sleeper Express between Varanasi and New Delhi from Banaras Railway Station today. In addition, two new MEMU train services connecting Varanasi will also be introduced to enhance rail connectivity in the region. Here is a report:

 

“Divisional Railway Manager of Varanasi, Ashish Jain informed that the new Vande Bharat Sleeper train will operate six days a week. It will depart from Varanasi at 8:50 PM and reach New Delhi at 6:10 AM next day. In the return, it will leave New Delhi at 9:40 PM and arrive in Varanasi at 7:10 AM. The train will have stoppages at Prayagraj, Kanpur Central, Aligarh and Ghaziabad. The DRM further informed that two new MEMU train will also be introduced. The first one will operate between Varanasi City Railway Station and Rajatalab, while the second will connect Prayagraj Rambagh with Varanasi. The new services are expected to improve rail connectivity and provide greater convenience to local passengers. Om Awasthi, Akashvani News Lucknow.”

The government has constituted a High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat to review the country’s banking sector and recommend reforms in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The Finance Ministry said, the Committee will recommend structural, institutional, regulatory and legislative reforms to make the Indian banking sector globally competitive, financially inclusive and resilient. The Committee will be chaired by former Central Vigilance Commissioner Suresh N. Patel.

“The High level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat  will have a tenure of six months. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had announced the setting up of the Committee in her Budget speech this year. The Committee will assess existing banking practices and prudential norms, identify global best practices and examine their suitability for adoption in the Indian banking system. It will also review the existing regulatory and legal frameworks governing banks, including Regional Rural Banks and Cooperative Banks, and suggest reforms to improve efficiency and ease of banking. In addition, the Committee will prepare a roadmap for the adoption of artificial intelligence and digital innovations in banking institutions, while recommending safeguards against cyber risks. With Rishu Jaiswal, Shivang Misra, Akashavni News, Delhi.”

President Droupadi Murmu will be on a two-day visit to Maharashtra and Haryana from today. The President will grace the Dhwaj Stambh Pujan, Dhawaja Pujan and Dhwajarohan ceremony of Simhastha Maha Kumbh at Maharashtra’s Nashik today. She will also address a public programme on the occasion.
Tomorrow, President Murmu will grace the ‘Hirak Jayanti’ celebration on the 60th year of formation of the state of Haryana at Kurukshetra. She will also grace the annual festival commemorating the Centenary of the sacrifice of Swami Shraddhanand Ji at Gurukul in Kurukshetra.

 

 

<><><> 

 

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has successfully launched its next-generation navigation satellite, NVS-03, marking a significant step towards strengthening the country’s indigenous satellite navigation capabilities. The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle, GSLV-F18, carrying the satellite, lifted off from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, last night.  NVS-03 is the third satellite in ISRO’s second-generation navigation satellite series. It is designed to ensure continuity and improve the availability of navigation services under the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), country’s indigenous alternative to the Global Positioning System (GPS).  Speaking to media later, Dr Narayanan said ISRO has placed its third indigenous atomic clock in orbit aboard the NVS-03 navigation satellite.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated the scientists, engineers and the entire team of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 rocket carrying the NVS-03 satellite.

The government has extended the existing customs duty exemption on cotton imports till the 31st of December this year. The Finance Ministry has issued a notification in this regard. The exemption, which was earlier valid until the 31st of October, has been extended to ensure adequate availability of cotton for the Indian textile sector. The extension is expected to reduce input costs across the textile and apparel industries, providing relief to manufacturers and consumers while safeguarding the interests of domestic farmers.

 India has asserted that military solutions cannot resolve global challenges and that diplomacy must be given an opportunity to address conflicts. Speaking at the first plenary session of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting at Atlanta in the United States, last night, External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar stressed the need to preserve freedom of navigation and ensure an end to attacks on civilian shipping and seafarers, in accordance with international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, UNCLOS. His remarks come amid ongoing conflicts in different parts of the world, including the Russia-Ukraine war and escalating tensions in West Asia. Dr Jaishankar said countries of the Global South are disproportionately bearing the consequences of attacks on civilian shipping and seafarers.

In Hockey, India registered its third consecutive victory at the ongoing Men’s Asian Champions Trophy, defeating Japan 4-1 at Jalandhar in Punjab, last evening. India produced an impressive performance, with Abhishek Nain emerging as the star of the match. He scored two field goals and was adjudged the Player of the Match. With this victory, India maintained its winning run in the tournament, having won all three of its matches so far.

“Seeing Indian players playing and countering Japan’s moves under the leadership of Sarpanch Sahib Capt. Harmanpreet Singh. India striked thrice within 9 minutes and took an unassailable lead from Japan. With this win, India is leading the pool standings with 9 points.
Malaysia is also having 9 points with 3 consective wins after thrashing Bangladesh by 6-1.in the first match of the day. In another match, South Korea registered its first win after beating China by 2-1. With this, Korea has earmed 3 points whereas China is yet to open its account.
Today is rest day. Tomorrow on November 1st, India will take on Malaysia, South Korea will face Bangladesh and China will try to open its account against Japan. Rajesh Bali, Jalandhar.”

India’s men’s and women’s teams have stormed into the finals of the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship being held in Ahmedabad. the Indian men’s team stormed into the final with a dominant 56-27 win over Bangladesh in the semi-finals. In the other semi-final, Sri Lanka defeated Kenya 28-24. The men’s final between India and Sri Lanka will take place at 9 PM today.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be on a two-day visit to Gujarat, beginning today. Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over 14 thousand crore rupees in Banaskantha today. The Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of Ahmedabad Metro Phase-2A (Airport Extension) and Phase-2B (GIFT City Extension). Mr Modi will also release the 24th instalment under PM-KISAN, amounting to 19 thousand crore rupees. He will also visit the Embryo Transfer Technology-In Vitro Fertilisation Laboratory and the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre cattle farm in Banaskantha.

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will attend various programs in Banaskantha, Ahmedabad and Ekta Nagar today on the first day of his Gujarat tour. Mr. Modi will dedicate the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre in Banaskantha to the nation. Spread over 127 acres, this state-of-the-art center of excellence will strengthen cattle breeding, genetic upgradation and advanced reproductive technology, speeding up the breeding process by 10 to 20 times. It will be the first facility in the country dedicated to the breeding of Kankrej cows. Additionally, the Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone for two Bio-CNG plants of Banas Dairy at Tharad and Radhanpur. Following his Banaskantha visit, Mr. Modi will lay the foundation stone for Phase-2A (Airport Extension) and Phase-2B (GIFT City Extension) of the Ahmedabad Metro Train. He will also lay the foundation stone to widen the Ahmedabad–Mehsana Road from four lanes to eight lanes at an estimated cost of ₹2,600 crore. Later in the evening, Mr. Modi will inaugurate ‘Bharat Parv 2026’ at Ekta Nagar—running through November 15—and participate in the ‘Ekta Prakash Parv’ and Narmada MahaAarti. Pravesh Adiacha, Akashvani News, Ahmedabad.

The Election Commission has extended the schedule for the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Haryana, Nagaland, and Delhi.

 

According to the poll body, in Maharashtra, the period for filing claims and objections has been extended till the 13th of next month. The notice phase, or disposal of claims and objections, will continue till 25th November. In Nagaland, the notice phase, or disposal of claims and objections, will also continue till 25th of November. In Andhra Pradesh and Haryana, the notice phase, or disposal of claims and objections, will continue till 20th of November. In Telangana, the notice phase, or disposal of claims and objections, will continue till the 26th of next month. The final publication of electoral rolls will take place in all five states on 30th November. In Delhi, the period for filing claims and objections has been extended till the 25th of next month. The notice phase, or disposal of claims and objections, will continue till 15th December. with Anupam Mishra, Nitika Gupta Akashvani News Delhi.

Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) will launch the navigation satellite NVS-03 aboard the GSLV-F18 rocket at 11:51 PM IST tonight. The liftoff will take place from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh. This mission marks the 20th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV). The rocket will deploy the satellite into a Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO). NVS-03 is the third, second-generation navigation satellite designed to maintain and boost the continuity of the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC) system. To enhance precise positioning, the satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock alongside procured ones. The NavIC system provides positioning, navigation, and timing services covering the Indian mainland and up to 1,500 km beyond its borders. A successful deployment tonight will restore NavIC’s basic operational requirements to four satellites, laying the groundwork for upcoming NVS-04 and NVS-05 launches to fully stabilize India’s independent navigation capabilities.

The 14th edition of the International Tourism Mart (ITM) began at Tawang in Arunachal Pradesh yesterday. The three-day Mart is aimed at showcasing the tourism potential of the eight North Eastern States and strengthen business engagement with domestic and international tourism markets.

Arunachal Pradesh Government has debunked a viral social media video claiming Chinese military vehicles entered Indian territory in the state, dismissing the content as misleading. The Indian Army’s Fact Check unit clarified that the trucks are authorised commercial vehicles operating under existing India-China bilateral trade agreements.

The Depression (Remnant of Cyclonic Storm “Arnab”) over central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha has moved nearly northwards and weakened into a Well Marked Low Pressure Area over central parts of Chhattisgarh. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said that it is very likely to continue to move north-northeastwards, and weaken further into a low pressure area over Northeast Chhattisgarh and neighbourhood by today evening. IMD has issued a red colour warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall over Bihar today.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The impact of Cyclonic Storm ‘Arnab’ has intensified in Bihar. Several parts of the state have been experiencing rainfall since yesterday. India Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for 32 districts, including Patna, for today. A Red Alert has been issued for Madhubani and Sitamarhi districts, where extremely heavy rainfall is likely. Orange and Yellow Alerts have been issued for other districts of the state. Meteorological Department has also warned of thunderstorms with wind speeds of 40 to 50 kilometres per hour, along with the possibility of lightning strikes.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Floods triggered by incessant torrential post-cyclone rainfall have severely affected Ganjam and Gajapati districts of Odisha, with Aska, Dharakote, Sorada and Bhanjanagar among the worst-hit areas. Hundreds of villages have been affected, while thousands remain marooned, prompting large-scale rescue and evacuation operations. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi along with a few other ministers will undertake an aerial survey of Ganjam and Gajapati today to assess the situation.

 

 

The Indian Coast Guard has launched helicopter rescue operations to evacuate people stranded in inaccessible Ganjam and Gajapati villages, while NDRF, ODRAF and Fire Service personnel are engaged in rescue and relief operations. The Rushikulya river is flowing above the danger mark at several locations, inundating villages and low-lying areas. Berhampur, Aska and Bhanjanagar have also reported waterlogging. More than one thousand villages have been badly affected by the current flood. A Central team is expected to arrive soon in Odisha to assess the damage due to Cyclone Arnab. East Coast Railway has cancelled nine trains and diverted fourteen others because railway tracks and bridges flooded. Educational institutions in Ganjam and Gajapati will remain closed till tomorrow, while schools and colleges in flood-hit Sundargarh district are also closed today. The IMD has forecast thunderstorms and lightning in parts of Odisha today, with heavy rain likely at isolated places along the south Odisha coast. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Flood fears have also gripped Alipurduar and Cooch Behar districts of West Bengal following reports of a glacial lake outburst flood in Bhutan. Both districts have been placed on high alert. According to reports, a lake burst following heavy rainfall in Bhutan, releasing nearly 74 lakh cubic metres of water into the Mo Chhu, or Sankosh river. The sudden surge could affect areas along the Sankosh river, including parts of the Buxa Tiger Reserve.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Meanwhile in Uttarakhand Disaster Management Department has directed officials concerned to remain on high alert following an orange alert for heavy rainfall in five districts of the state. The Meteorological Department has forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places in Nainital, Champawat, Pithoragarh, Bageshwar and Chamoli districts today. A yellow alert has also been issued for the remaining districts, warning of lightning and strong gusty winds. Disaster Management and Rehabilitation Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman has asked officials to maintain special vigilance along the Char Dham pilgrimage routes and ensure that pilgrims are moved to safe locations in case of adverse weather conditions or any potential threat.

The Nationwide Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5.0 is being organised from 1st to 30th November 2026. This campaign aims to digitise the process of submitting life certificates through Aadhaar biometrics and other mediums. This campaign aims to reach pensioners across 2,000 cities and towns. Speaking exclusively to Akashvani News, Nivedita Sukla Verma, Secretary of the Department of Pension and Pensioner’s Welfare, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions highlighted the details of this campaign. She also encouraged maximum number of pensioners to participate in the same.

 

Listen to the full interview in our daily programme, Spotlight, tonight at 9:15 PM on Akashvani FM Gold, 100.1 MHz.

In Hockey, India continued their winning streak at Men’s Hero Asian Champions Trophy by defeating China 5-2 in their second league match at Jalandhar in Punjab last evening. The Indian team maintained its momentum despite a strong attacking display by China.  In all the three intense and high powered encounters at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey stadium, besides hosts India, Japan and Malaysia also registered victories.

 

In the most thrilling and high octane clash between India and China, the Indian team proved its mettle in the field despite continued attempts by China to over ride Capt Harmanpreet’s team. The Indian skipper’s talismanic drag flicks found the net twice as he converted two penalty corners into goals. Jugraj Singh also did the same to find the opposing team’s net through a penalty corner whereas Sukhjeet Singh scored 2 wonderful field goals.  For China, both the goals scored through penalty corners. In other two matchs, Japan just managed to scrape through against a spirited Bangladesh by 1-0. Whereas, Malaysia beat South Korea by 3-1. In today’s fixtures, India will take on Japan, Bangladesh will face Malaysia and South Korea will do dribbling with China. Rajesh Bali, Akashvani News, Jalandhar.

THE HEADLINES:

 

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi reviews infrastructure projects worth over 16,000 crore rupees across 31 States and Union Territories at 54th PRAGATI meeting.
  2. Union Cabinet approves 3 percent hike in Dearness Allowance for central government employees.
  3. Cyclonic storm Arnab weakens into deep depression and likely to further weaken into a depression this morning.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the 54th meeting of PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth in New Delhi yesterday. During the meeting, the  Prime Minister reviewed infrastructure projects across the Railways, Ekta Malls and Drug Parks worth over 16 thousand crore rupees covering 31 States and Union Territories. More from our correspondent:

 

“Pivotal to economic growth and public welfare, these projects, were reviewed with a focus on timeliness, inter-agency coordination, and timely issue resolution. Prime Minister asked the concerned Ministries and State Governments to resolve bottlenecks in mission mode, strengthen Centre-State and inter-agency coordination, and ensure close monitoring at the senior-most level. Calling for a proactive work culture with greater ownership at every level, he stressed the need to anticipate implementation challenges, take timely decisions and fix clear accountability for completing projects on schedule.

 

Prime Minister Modi asked Chief Secretaries to review schemes with District Magistrates monthly to address implementation gaps and ensure timely delivery of benefits. He also emphasised on regular monitoring and timely completion of PM Ekta Malls to promote local products, support artisans and expand their enterprises. With Anand Kumar, Dilnashi Arzoo, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi has approved three percent increase in Dearness Allowance to Central Government employees and Dearness Relief to Pensioners with effect from 1st of July, 2026. Briefing media after the Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said this will benefit over 48 lakh Central Government employees and 68 lakh pensioners.

 

Mr Vaishnaw said, Cabinet has approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme with a total outlay of ten thousand crore rupees over 13 years. He said the scheme aims to establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India.

Mr Vaishnaw said, Cabinet has also given nod to the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme to position India as a global hub for high-quality sports goods.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah has called on President Droupadi Murmu at Rashrapati Bhawan in New Delhi. He informed about the meeting through a social media post.

Cyclonic Storm ‘Arnab’, which was moving over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and the adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal, has weakened into a deep depression. It is very likely to weaken further into a Depression by the morning and a well-marked low-pressure area by the evening today. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned fishermen not to venture into northwest Bay of Bengal and along and off West Bengal Coast today.

 

<><><> 

 

Cyclone Arnab has caused extensive damage to crops, houses, roads and power infrastructure across several districts of Andhra Pradesh. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has requested the Centre to send an inter-ministerial team for an early assessment of the losses. The State Government has intensified relief and restoration operations in the affected areas. More from our correspondent:

 

“Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviewed cyclone relief operations through the State’s Real-Time Governance Centre and directed officials to expedite restoration of essential services. The Chief Minister announced an ex-gratia of five lakh rupees each to the families of those who lost their lives and financial assistance to affected households. Preliminary estimates indicate damage to over 70 thousand hectares of paddy and more than 10 thousand hectares of horticultural crops. Over 28 thousand people have been evacuated to relief shelters, with NDRF and SDRF teams deployed across affected districts. Electricity restoration is progressing, with nearly 80 percent of power supply restored in Visakhapatnam district. Repair work is continuing in Konaseema, Kakinada and the Godavari districts, where fallen trees and damaged electricity poles disrupted services. Officials are also clearing blocked roads and restoring drinking water supplies. Meanwhile, the Chief Minister has requested Centre to send a team to assess cyclone-related losses. R. Sai Gireesh, for Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

 

<><><> 

 

Even as Cyclone Arnab has weakened further, its impact continues to be felt across southern Odisha, where torrential rain has triggered flood-like conditions. Ganjam and Gajapati districts are among the worst affected, with rising rivers, inundated villages and disruption of road connectivity. The India Meteorological Department has forecast further heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in several districts of Odisha today. More from our Correspondent:

 

“Heavy rainfall has severely affected normal life in Ganjam and neighbouring Gajapati districts. Ganjam, Chhatrapur, Digapahandi and Berhampur recorded substantial rainfall, while Mahendragiri in Gajapati received nearly 250 millimetres in 24 hours. Flooding in the Ghodahada river has inundated villages and disrupted road connectivity, with parts of National Highway 326 also affected. Villages in Sorada and other vulnerable areas face connectivity problems. The Rushikulya and Bahuda river basins remain under close watch, while rising reservoir levels have prompted monitoring and water releases. Many villages are inundated due to the floodwater of Rushikulay. Authorities are monitoring flood-prone areas and restoring essential services .The IMD has issued heavy rain in several districts of Odisha today. All schools and anganwadi centres in Kalahandi, Kandhamal and Subarnapur districts are closed today as very heavy rain is expected there. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

Normalcy is gradually returning to the cyclone-affected coastal villages of Yanam following the passage of Cyclone Arnab yesterday. Restoration work is underway to repair the damage caused by strong winds and seawater intrusion. A report:

 

“Several areas in Yanam suffered damage to electrical infrastructure, with 65 electric poles dismantled, two transformers damaged and around 15 kilometres of electrical lines affected. Approximately 101 acres of paddy crops have also been damaged. Officials of Electricity department along with Yanam administration and emergency response teams are engaged in clearing fallen trees, restoring electricity and reopening roads blocked by debris. Road blockages caused by fallen trees along the 17-kilometre Yanam-Savitri Nagar road were completely cleared yesterday. In Savitri Nagar, where seawater entered houses, residents have started returning from relief camps to clean their homes. Food and other essential supplies are being provided to them at all 20 cyclone relief camps. Meanwhile, educational institutions in Yanam will remain closed today as a precautionary measure. With inputs from K Sheshu Babu, Bibin S Nath, Akashvani News, Puducherry,”

The Minister further said that Indian farmers are becoming important players in the production of Hydrogen and other valuable energy products and contributing in reducing India’s need for importing these materials. Mr Gadkari also said that with increasing Hydrogen production, India can become an energy exporting country in the future.

The US Federal Reserve has kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at a target range of 3.75% to 4.00%, keeping the average effective rate at approximately 3.9%. More from our correspondent:

 

“Led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) opted to maintain the status quo following a quarter-percentage-point hike in September, which had marked the central bank’s first interest rate increase in three years. The decision was not unanimous. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented from the hold, voting to raise the target range by a quarter percentage point due to persistent inflation concerns. The central bank stated that keeping rates unchanged allows for the “accumulation of more information” to ensure a timely return of inflation to its 2% target. The decision comes less than a week before the US midterm elections. Financial markets and economists continue to anticipate a potential final quarter-point rate hike at the next FOMC meeting scheduled for 8th and 9th December 2026. KAUMUDEE PAREEK, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

The very severe cyclonic storm Arnab has commenced its landfall process along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts near Kakinada. According to India Meteorological Department (IMD), the landfall process started at 1:20 AM today. The crossing began earlier than originally expected due to the rapid movement of the storm. The storm hit the coast packing sustained maximum wind speeds of 115-125 km per hour, with gusts reaching up to 140 km per hour.

 

Heavy rainfall and strong winds have disrupted normal life across several coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh.

 

“Cyclone Arnab remained practically stationary near the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts, south of Yanam. Extremely heavy rainfall has lashed several coastal districts, with Kannuripalem in Anakapalli district recording 259 millimetres of rainfall. Strong winds reaching 130 kilometres per hour were recorded at Maruteru, while uprooted trees, power disruptions and flooding have affected normal life in several areas. The state government is closely monitoring the situation, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviewing relief operations with district collectors and disaster management officials. More than 84 thousand people have been evacuated to 290 relief shelters, while NDRF teams remain deployed in affected areas. Train and flight services have been disrupted, with several cancellations and rescheduling of services. Authorities have warned of storm surges up to two-and-a-half metres, particularly near Kakinada and Yanam, and advised residents of vulnerable coastal and low-lying areas to remain alert. R. Sai Gireesh, for Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

 

In Puducherry, normal life has been affected in the coastal region of Yanam as cyclonic storm Arnab began making landfall near Kakinada in the early hours of this morning.

 

“Strong winds uprooted trees and electric poles, disrupting power supply in several areas. Seawater entered several houses in coastal villages of Yanam. Residents have been shifted to 19 cyclone relief centres opened in the region.

 

Around 300 personnel, including Puducherry Police, India Reserve Battalion and the National Disaster Response Force, have been deployed in the region for rescue and relief operations.

Puducherry Public Works Minister Malladi Krishna Rao and Regional Administrator Sivaraj Meena visited the affected areas  and assured residents of all necessary assistance. With K Sheshu Babu, Bibin S Nath, Akashvani News, Puducherry.”

 

Heavy rain and strong winds have lashed southern Odisha under the influence of cyclonic storm Arnab. Rain continues in Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Malkangiri and Nabarangpur, with rainfall intensity likely to increase today. The IMD has issued a red warning for five districts and an orange warning for several other parts of the state. Odisha is maintaining heightened preparedness, with the Chief Minister scheduled to monitor the post-landfall situation from the Special Relief Commissioner’s office.

 

“Southern Odisha continues to experience heavy rain and strong winds under the influence of very severe cyclonic storm Arnab, which is crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast. In Odisha, Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Malkangiri and Nabarangpur are among the districts facing severe weather and red warnning has been issued for these districts for today by  the India Meteorological Department (IMD). Port town Gopalpur recorded the highest rainfall in the state over the last 24 hours, according to the available information. No casualty has been reported in Odisha so far. The state government is closely monitoring the situation, with Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and the Revenue Minister scheduled to review post-landfall developments at the Special Relief Commissioner’s office. Authorities have shifted more than one lakh people living in vulnerable areas to safer locations. A number of trains have been cancelled or routes have been diverte for today, while bus services southern districts from other parts of the state have been completely suspended. Fishing activities remain suspended as the sea continues to be very rough. Prakash Dash for Akashvnai News, Bhubaneswar.”

 

Continuous rainfall since last night has affected Ranchi and several other parts of Jharkhand due to Cyclone Arnab. Meteorological Department has issued an orange alert for heavy rainfall and strong winds.

 

“Intermittent rainfall has been continuing since last night in Ranchi and several parts of Jharkhand under the influence of Cyclone Arnab. According to the Meteorological Department, heavy to very heavy rainfall accompanied by winds reaching speeds of 60 kilometres per hour is likely in Ranchi, Khunti, Gumla and the entire Kolhan division today and tomorrow.

As a precautionary measure, all schools in Ranchi and the Kolhan division have been closed for these two days.

 

Rail services have also been affected. The Railways has cancelled or short-terminated several trains, including the Bhubaneswar-Jagdalpur, Howrah-Jagdalpur and Rourkela-Jagdalpur Express. Air passengers have also been advised to check their flight status.

 

The administration has advised people to stay away from trees and electric poles during adverse weather conditions. Farmers have also been advised to secure harvested crops and ensure proper drainage in their fields. Mahvish Rahman, Akashvani News, Ranchi.”

Parliamentary election in Israel remained deadlocked, with exit polls from all three major television networks giving opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc a narrow two-seat lead over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp. The projections put Eisenkot’s bloc at 52 seats and Netanyahu’s Likud-led alliance at 50, leaving neither side with the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member parliament-Knesset.

 

“The results could give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, but his path to power remains uncertain. The remaining 18 seats were projected to go to Arab parties not aligned with either bloc, and Eisenkot has largely ruled out forming a government with them. Netanyahu, meanwhile, could remain caretaker prime minister if coalition talks fail.

 

Israel’s Central Elections Committee said, voters turnout reached 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades and around seven percentage points above the 2022 election. The vote was the first since the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

 

Netanyahu has served as prime minister for nearly 19 of the past 30 years and has repeatedly survived political crises. His opponents removed him from office only once since 2009, but he returned to power 18 months later.

With the latest exit polls showing a narrow advantage for Eisenkot’s bloc but no clear majority for either side, the final count and subsequent coalition negotiations will determine who can form Israel’s next government. Kaumudee Pareek, Akashvani News.”

The Election Commission has defended its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls before the Supreme Court, maintaining that the exercise was authorised by law and the relevant orders were approved unanimously by all three members of the Commission. Rejecting the allegations that Form 6 had been amended, the poll panel said that no changes were made to the statutory Form 6 used for voter registration. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant is scheduled to hear on Tuesday petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the decisions taken by the poll panel during the SIR. In a counter affidavit, the poll body sought summary dismissal of the petitions and called the allegations misconceived which rested on a single newspaper report. It said the affidavit itself has been approved for filing by a unanimous decision of all three members of the Commission.

The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum will commence in New Delhi from today. The theme of the two-day event is “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development.” Prime Minister Narendra Modi will grace the event and will meet the leaders of the visiting delegations. Eleven BRICS Member countries and 10 Partner countries have been invited for the event. Parliamentary delegations from these countries will participate in the meeting. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

         

 

 

“Lok Sabha Speaker and Chairperson of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum Om Birla will preside over the proceedings and hold discussions with leaders of the visiting delegations during the bilateral meetings. Building on the legacy of the BRICS Parliamentary Forum, the 12th Forum aims to foster consensus-based dialogue through four High-Level Sessions based on Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. A dedicated meeting of the Chairs of International Affairs Committees of Parliaments of BRICS Member and Partner countries will be held to deliberate on parliamentary diplomacy, capacity-building, and sharing of best practices. The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum, being hosted by India, will provide an opportunity to advance parliamentary diplomacy, strengthen democratic institutions, and promote cooperation among member and partner countries. Akshit Vedyan, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has said that the use of terrorism as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable, and it can never be justified or rationalised. He said, terrorism continues because not all states display zero tolerance for the menace. Dr Jaishankar was addressing an event held in New Delhi to mark 75th anniversary of Chinmaya Mission. He said, the world must develop sharper awareness about this common threat, and it must come together with stronger resolve to counter terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.

 

 

 

         

 

 

He underlined the importance of peace, especially amid the ongoing conflicts in the world, and cautioned that war anywhere threatens peace everywhere. Dr Jaishankar cited the two major conflicts going on in the world, in Ukraine and in West Asia, and said societies and economies and people far away who have little say in the matter are actually paying the cost.

ISRO Chairman V Narayanan has said that India will expand its space operations significantly with four functional launch pads by the year 2029. Mr. Narayanan said, these include a 2 thousand acre dedicated Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) complex at Kulasekarapattinam in Tuticorin district of Tamil Nadu and a third launch pad at Sriharikota, to meet the global demand for satellite launches. He was addressing convocation of a private university at Porur near Chennai.

 

 

 

         

 

 

The ISRO chief said that the upcoming Kulasekarapattinam spaceport facility will feature crucial infrastructure such as integration buildings, launch pads, rail-track systems, telemetry, tracking, and command systems.

 

 

         

 

Mr. Narayanan stated that ISRO plans to conduct the first uncrewed Gaganyaan test within the next two months, followed by two subsequent uncrewed tests before the crewed mission.

India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the Deep Depression over Bay of Bengal will intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm today. IMD has advised the fisherman not to venture into West central and adjoining Northwest and Southwest Bay of Bengal during the next two days.

 

 

Talking to Akashvani News, Director General of IMD, Dr Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said, due to influence of depression the sea condition is very rough and will deteriorate further. He said that the wind speed may lead to large scale damage of structures and standing crops. He said that heavy to extremely heavy rainfall may hit parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh during the next two days. Dr Mohapatra added that due to heavy rainfall can cause flooding in low-lying areas and landslides in hilly areas and urged the people living in these regions to be cautious.

In Brazil, Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has defeated right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil’s intense presidential race. With this victory, Lula has become the only politician in modern Brazilian history who successfully rebound and win the second round after falling behind in the first. A report:

 

 

         

 

 

“Incumbent Lula won the final runoff election with 51 percent of the vote and more than 51.49 million ballots. Meanwhile, Bolsonaro received 48.68 percent of the vote, which amounted to 48.8 million ballots. Just over 2.6 million votes separated the two candidates. Because of the close and highly contested race, voting stations across the country remained open two hours longer than originally planned.

         

 

 

The former metalworker union leader, at the age of 80 will be sworn into office on 5th of January next year, breaking his own record as the oldest president to take the oath of office since Brazil returned to a democracy. This victory marks an unprecedented fourth non-consecutive term for Lula, who has run for the presidency a total of seven times. KAUMUDEE PAREEK FOR AKASHVANI NEWS DELHI.”
